title: Clew connector protocol
description: Shapes exchanged between Clew and a connector service. See docs/reference/connector-protocol.md.

protocol.description: The version of this contract the manifest is written to, not of the connector (D60). This instance loads 2; an additive change to the protocol keeps the number.

id.description: Stable and lowercase. Must match the id Clew was configured with, and prefixes every capability name.

kind.description: Who owns the data (D3): `passthrough` when it lives in the connected system and Clew keeps refs and audit rows only; `derived` when the connector computes it from other sources. `core` is Clew's own and never a remote connector.

source.description: Swedish. The system as shown on cards: "Personalsystemet".

areas.description: The areas this connector gives a person: each is a button under the box on Hem (D41, D53) with its standing actions, schedules and figure. Empty is allowed for a connector that only answers questions.

id.description: Stable and lowercase. It is the area's address, `/areas/<id>`, and what a scan draft names in `area`.

title.description: Swedish. The area's name on its button under the box and in the sidebar.

roles.description: Who sees the area: at least one role.

standing.description: Capability names shown under "Gör själv": what a person can do here without composing a question. Each must be a capability of this manifest.

schedules.description: What the connector does for this area on its own and when, as a person reads it under the area. Informational text; the scan itself runs nightly and on first visit.

label.description: Swedish. What happens: "Nya saker att göra".

figure.description: Clew asks POST /clew/figure for this area's figure and draws it as a tile on Hem (D54), unless an administrator switched it off.

icon.description: One of Clew's icons. The connector sends a name, never a drawing.

capabilities.description: What the connector can do, one entry per operation. The name is the contract (D37): a break is a new name, never a changed one.

execution.description: How a write may be repeated safely after a lost answer (D45): `manual`, `deduplicated` (operation ids kept for `retentionSeconds`, found by `lookup`) or `conditional` (`lookup` tells whether the effect holds). Omitted means manual. Only meaningful on an `execute`.

strategy.description: Clew never repeats a write by itself; a lost answer is an unknown outcome a person resolves.
The source keeps the operation id Clew sends in `X-Clew-Operation-Id` and answers a repeat with the original result.

retentionSeconds.description: How long, in seconds, the source remembers an operation id.

lookup.description: This connector's read that takes `{ operationId }` and answers `{ found, result? }`, so Clew can establish what happened before it decides to replay.

strategy.description: The source writes only when its revision still matches, and `lookup` tells whether the effect already holds.

lookup.description: This connector's read that tells whether the effect already holds.

name.description: `<connector id>.<verb>`, stable. Two names are profiles Clew combines across connectors: `<id>.search` (D26, see `kinds`), and `<id>.errands` (D35, D89), a read that takes `{ view?: "assigned" | "reported" }` and answers an ErrandsOutput with the errands the case system lets the person see. Its view's `open` names the read that shows one errand, by convention `<id>.errand`. Clew lists every `<id>.errands` in the person's scope as `clew.errands`. Two more are the talks profile (D96), answered by one system per installation rather than combined: `<id>.talks`, a read that takes `{}` and answers a TalksOutput (the open round of development talks and one row per person the reader manages, keyed on the SCIM `userName`), and `<id>.commitments`, a read that takes `{ person?: <userName> }` and answers a CommitmentsOutput (that employee's action points for a manager of their unit, or without `person` the ones the reader owns and the ones about the reader). `<id>.talks` may be limited to managers; `<id>.commitments` should be callable by everyone who owns action points or is their subject. Clew's built-in `talks` connector answers while either of its reads is enabled for the person; otherwise the one connector whose `<id>.talks` or `<id>.commitments` the person may call does, and with several none does. Neither is ever offered to the model.

kind.description: `read` answers; `propose` drafts something for a person to decide; `execute` changes the source and runs only after a human decision (D8), never as a tool and never through a callback.

title.description: Swedish. A button label.

description.description: Swedish. What the model reads when `model` is true.

input.description: JSON Schema of the input. Clew validates a call against it before the connector sees it. `required` properties mean the capability needs input, which keeps it out of the menu and out of the conformance check's calls.

output.description: JSON Schema of the output. Clew validates the answer against it; where it declares `properties`, a view's keys must be among them (D38).

model.description: Offer it to the model as a tool, once an administrator has enabled tools for the connector. Must be false for execute (D8).

scope.description: Who may call the capability at all. Omitted roles means every signed-in person. The connector narrows further in the call.

roles.description: `manager`, `employee` or both. Omitted means both. A role outside the list is refused before the connector is called.

kinds.description: For `<id>.search` (D26): what it can find. Its output is a SearchOutput; `<id>.fetch` takes one of its refs back and returns one SearchHit.

view.description: How Clew draws the output: `table` and `list` over an array of records (`rows`, default "rows"; `title` names the field that names a row and is one of `fields`; `ref` the field holding the connector's ref), `detail` over one record, `text` over one Markdown string.

format.description: How the value is drawn: `phone` and `email` become links that call and write, `link` an http(s) link out, `date` and `instant` are formatted in Swedish, `number` is aligned as one, `status` is a badge with a tone from `tones`. Default `text`.

tones.description: For `status`: the tone per value (a yes/no value is keyed `true` and `false`). The key `*` is the tone of any other value that is present, so a count such as "2 försenade" can warn while an absent value stays neutral (D97). A value without one is neutral; give a tone only to the value that needs the person.

unit.description: For `number`: the unit drawn after the value, so a row reads "12 platser" and never "Platser: 12". Only where the unit alone says what the number is.

other.description: Swedish. The word after any other number: "platser".

beside.description: Drawn in the same cell or on the same line as the field before it, under that field's label: a state and its time ("Bokat", "tors 12 nov kl. 09:00"), a count and what is late in it ("3 öppna", "2 försenade"). Never on the first field (D97).

compact.description: The row in one value ("tors 12 nov", "Inte bokat"): drawn where there is room for one value, a column on a list or a one-line summary, and left out where the whole row is drawn, a lens, a section or a detail. At most one field of a view (D97).

menu.description: How this capability's view is named and marked when an administrator puts it in Clew's menu under Verktyg (D40). Only on a read that declares a view and needs no input.

about.description: What the rows concern (D97). A `read` takes `{ keys }` (an array of at most 200 strings, required) and answers `rows` (or its view's rows), one per key it knows, each with a string `key` it was asked with; a key outside the caller's scope is answered as no row, never as a refusal. It declares a `table` or `list` view, is never a tool (`model: false`), and may answer `heading` and `note`, two strings beside the rows. A `propose` or `execute` names in `param` the input property that takes one key. Clew decides where it shows: an action in the entity's menu, a read as a section on the opened entity, a `warn` or `alert` tone as a mark on its row, a table or list as a lens an administrator may offer.

entity.description: `person`: a person in the directory, keyed on their provisioned `userName`. `unit`: a unit, keyed on its id.

param.description: On a `propose` or `execute` only: the string property of the input that takes the key of the one entity it acts on. A read takes its keys in `keys` and declares none.

follows.description: For a `propose` (D55): the fact kinds it answers for. Input is a FactEnvelope, output a FollowResponse; steps name this connector only.

items.description: `<connector id>:<kind>`, stable: the name is the contract.

creates.description: The fact kind this `propose` or `execute` brings about (D55); must be one of the manifest's `facts`.

uses.description: The exact capability names of other connectors this one calls back through `POST /api/connectors/call` while serving a request (D37), such as `calendar.today`. A name not listed is refused; an `execute` can never be called back.

facts.description: The fact kinds this connector creates (D55), each prefixed with its id.

attributes.description: JSON Schema of the fact's attributes. A follower receives exactly these; a new optional attribute keeps the kind, anything else is a new kind (D37).

When several enabled connectors declare one, the earliest registered answers. Clew keeps no header of its own beyond its default (the site's name and Start).
